habitat: Humid to subhumid woodlands and gallery forests.
summary: Wikipedia distinguishes this cuckoo from other brood parasites by its very thick, hawk-like bill. The page used does not describe the plumage or the voice. In its southernmost range it is partially migratory and spends the southern dry season in East Africa. It parasitises helmetshrikes. Months were left unset. The Kemp code VB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Wikipedia separates Thick-billed Cuckoo from other brood-parasitic cuckoos by the very thick, hawk-like bill, not by a plumage description.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^5=32 mature individuals (visiting breeder); paper interval half–double → 16–64.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

bill.shape: Very thick, and shaped rather like a hawk’s bill.

viewNotes.note: The only mark given is the very thick, hawk-like bill. Plumage was not described.
The bill is very thick. Face and underpart colours were not described.
A flight pattern was not described. The bill is compared with a hawk’s.

calls.description: The Wikipedia page used here does not describe the voice. Grade A song from Dzalamyama, Malawi. The filename names Thick-billed Cuckoo. A Kruger alarm call is only grade B and has a generic filename, so it was not used.

research.note: No Newman page was found. Wikipedia describes the bill and the partial migration, not the plumage, the voice, or a total length, so size is omitted. Status is intra-african-migrant because the southern birds spend the dry season in East Africa, and months were left unset. Population figures were left unchanged.
